prompt:
A 0.60 kg cart moving at 2.0 m/s on a frictionless track collides head-on with a stationary 0.20 kg cart.

**(a)** Suppose the carts stick together after the collision. Calculate their common speed and the kinetic energy lost.

**(b)** Suppose instead that the collision is elastic. Write two equations that must be satisfied, and calculate the velocity of each cart after the collision.

**(c)** Use your answers to (b) to verify that kinetic energy is conserved in the elastic collision.

**(d)** In the elastic collision the carts are in contact for 0.020 s. Calculate the magnitude of the average force that the 0.60 kg cart exerts on the 0.20 kg cart.

rubric.description: (a) Uses momentum conservation to find $v=1.5$ m/s
(a) Finds the kinetic energy lost: $1.20-0.90=0.30$ J
(b) Writes conservation of momentum and conservation of kinetic energy (or the relative-speed condition)
(b) Finds $v_1=1.0$ m/s and $v_2=3.0$ m/s, both in the original direction
(c) Shows $\frac12(0.60)(1.0)^2+\frac12(0.20)(3.0)^2=1.20$ J equals the initial kinetic energy
(d) Finds the impulse on the small cart, $(0.20)(3.0)=0.60$ N$\cdot$s, and $F=\frac{0.60}{0.020}=30$ N

sampleResponse:
(a) $m_1v_1=(m_1+m_2)v$: $(0.60)(2.0)=(0.80)v$, so $v=1.5$ m/s. Initial $KE=\frac12(0.60)(2.0)^2=1.20$ J; final $KE=\frac12(0.80)(1.5)^2=0.90$ J. The energy lost is $0.30$ J.
(b) Momentum: $m_1v_1=m_1v_{1f}+m_2v_{2f}$. Kinetic energy: $\frac12m_1v_1^2=\frac12m_1v_{1f}^2+\frac12m_2v_{2f}^2$. Solving, $v_{1f}=\frac{m_1-m_2}{m_1+m_2}v_1=1.0$ m/s and $v_{2f}=\frac{2m_1}{m_1+m_2}v_1=3.0$ m/s, both in the original direction of motion.
(c) $KE_f=\frac12(0.60)(1.0)^2+\frac12(0.20)(3.0)^2=0.30+0.90=1.20$ J, equal to the initial 1.20 J.
(d) The impulse on the 0.20 kg cart is its change in momentum: $(0.20)(3.0)-0=0.60$ N$\cdot$s. $F_{avg}=\frac{J}{\Delta t}=\frac{0.60}{0.020}=30$ N.

prompt:
A tennis racket strikes a stationary 0.057 kg ball. The graph shows the force that the racket exerts on the ball as a function of time during the contact. The force is horizontal.

**(a)** Determine the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the ball.

**(b)** Calculate the speed of the ball just after it leaves the racket.

**(c)** Calculate the magnitude of the average force exerted on the ball during the 12 ms contact.

**(d)** The ball then strikes a vertical wall head-on and rebounds in the opposite direction at 40 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the impulse the wall exerts on the ball.

rubric.description: (a) Finds the area under the graph, $0.8+1.6+0.8=3.2$ N$\cdot$s (with the time axis converted from ms to s)
(b) Uses $J=m\,\Delta v$ with the ball starting at rest: $v\approx56$ m/s
(d) Takes opposite directions into account: $\Delta v=56+40$ m/s

sampleResponse:
(a) The area under the graph (time in seconds): triangle $\frac12(0.004)(400)=0.8$, rectangle $(0.004)(400)=1.6$, triangle $0.8$. Total: $3.2$ N$\cdot$s.
(b) $J=m\,\Delta v$ with $v_i=0$: $v=\frac{3.2}{0.057}\approx56$ m/s.
(c) $F_{avg}=\frac{J}{\Delta t}=\frac{3.2}{0.012}\approx2.7\times10^2$ N.
(d) The velocity reverses, so the change in velocity is $56+40=96$ m/s. $J=(0.057)(96)\approx5.5$ N$\cdot$s.

diagram.altText: Force versus time: rises from 0 to 400 N at t=4 ms, stays at 400 N until t=8 ms, then falls to 0 at t=12 ms.
